text:
leo_sales: Acme (Zoe) wants to run a 6-week air-gapped POC in their colo. Requirements: customer-side signing (HSM), minibundles weekly, full bundle monthly, strict no-key-escrow, estimated delta bandwidth ~40-60GB/week. Any immediate no-go items?

devon_se: We can support BYOK for Private installs. For POC the smoothest path is to hand them a signing helper that runs entirely inside their network and outputs a signed manifest. Need to confirm HSM vendor (YubiHSM vs. CloudHSM vs. nShield) for CLI options.

mira_infra: Packaging constraints: weekly diffs are fine if we produce chunked deltas and avoid shipping full model weights each time. However, driver/kernel pinning and custom fp16 kernels can inflate deltas. If they require pinned NVIDIA drivers across upgrades, expect larger size. Also we need their accepted checksum algorithm (sha256 vs sha512).

sam_sec: Security redlines from questionnaire: 1) Redwood must never hold private keys; 2) Signing must be reproducible with provided verification tooling; 3) Audit logs for signing operations. We can provide best-effort logs from the signing-tool (local) but they insist logs stay in-customer.

zoe_cust: Confirming: Acme will not allow outbound access from the POC cluster. They want a signing flow where we deliver a "packaging artifact" and they run the signing step in their HSM. Also need a documented rollback playbook — they want a zero-downtime fallback if a minibundle causes a failure.

ian_ops: Rollback nuance: if minibundle includes DB migrations, true automatic rollback is hard. We recommend only shipping non-destructive changes for weekly deltas and schedule any migration in the monthly full bundle with explicit maintenance window. For non-db changes we can support auto-rollback via our agent which verifies healthchecks post-deploy and reverts if failed.

devon_se: Two deployment options to propose: (A) signing-tool container + verify binary; we ship artifacts unsigned and customer signs locally. (B) a documented manual sign workflow where we provide scripts to compute manifest + detached sig. Option A is easier for customers.

packaging-bot: packaging-bot: created task PKG-2107: build signing-tool container + doc + verify tool.

leo_sales: Pricing question from Acme: will weekly minibundles incur an extra per-release handling fee? They anticipated an ops engineering charge. Thoughts?

devon_se: Standard approach: one-time packaging engineering fee (validate on their matrix + build signing-tool), plus a per-minibundle handling fee (covers QA + generation). For larger committed deals we usually amortize into a support retainer. I'll draft numbers.

sam_sec: Legal/contract note: add explicit SOW language: "Redwood will provide signing tooling only; customer retains exclusive control of private key material; Redwood shall never receive or persist private keys." Also add acceptance criteria for POC including preflight checklist sign-off.

mira_infra: Preflight checklist (short): disk >= 500GB, container runtime (docker/containerd) allowed, HSM access validated (slot/key label), kernel/driver matrix match, dry-run deploy on staging namespace, monitoring hooks installed. I'll author a one-pager.

zoe_cust: Can Redwood's signing-tool integrate with our offline HSM? We use Luna/HSM with middleware. We need examples for pkcs11 usage.

devon_se: We can add pkcs11 support to the tool. Example usage (to run inside customer network):

```
# sign inside the customer's airgapped environment
docker run --rm -v /acme/artifacts:/artifacts redwood/sign-helper:2026-03 \
  sign --bundle /artifacts/2026-03-minibundle.tar.gz \
  --pkcs11-module /usr/lib/libpkcs11.so --slot 1 --pin-file /run/hsm/pinfile \
  --out /artifacts/2026-03-minibundle.sig

# verify (redwood-provided tool)
redwood-verify --manifest /artifacts/manifest.json --sig /artifacts/2026-03-minibundle.sig
```

ian_ops: For rollback automation we'll include a health-check probe and a staged canary: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic revert on failure. That reduces blast radius and often eliminates full DB rollbacks.

leo_sales: Action items: @devon_se: repo + pkcs11 example + draft pricing. @mira_infra: preflight one-pager + size estimates for deltas and chunking. @sam_sec: SOW wording + audit log language. @zoe_cust: please confirm HSM vendor and whether Acme can run the signing container in a jump box. Meeting scheduled Fri 9am PT to review.

devon_se: I'll put a baseline price: one-time packaging fee $18k (engineering + 2 validation cycles), per-minibundle handling $600 each (includes QA + packaging). I'll refine after matrix test.

zoe_cust: Sounds reasonable, will review with procurement. One more ask: can we get a degraded-mode policy if they can't run weekly sign ops? e.g., accept pre-signed minibundles in a sealed staging bucket?

sam_sec: Degraded mode is OK only if there's a legally binding custodian transfer with signed attestation and an offline audit log. Prefer customers to sign themselves.

leo_sales: Great thread. I'll send the invite and include the PKG-2107 ticket in the agenda. We'll aim to close POC setup and pricing by EOW. :thumbsup:
